complete-kyrgyzstan-adventure-12-days: Twelve days that take in the whole country. Three days on horseback from Kyzart over the Jalgyz-Karagai pass and along Song-Kul, the Tash-Rabat caravanserai, an off-road day into Kok-Kiya and the walk to Kel-Suu. Then the south shore of Issyk-Kul and the trek from Altyn-Arashan up to Ala-Kul.
grand-kyrgyzstan-road-trip-12-days: Our longest drive, at an unhurried pace. From Kyzyl-Oi and Ak-Kol to two nights at Song-Kul, on to Tash-Rabat, Kok-Kiya and Kel-Suu, then Issyk-Kul, Altyn-Arashan, Karakol and Chong-Kemin. It ends with the Burana tower and a Bishkek city tour, and the only real walk is the 14 km to Kel-Suu.
tash-rabat-kel-suu-road-trip-11-days: Eleven days by road with a different start: through Kyzyl-Oi, Ak-Kol and Ming-Kush to Song-Kul, then south to the Tash-Rabat caravanserai, off-road to Kok-Kiya and on foot to Kel-Suu. The loop closes along Issyk-Kul with an off-road run up to Altyn-Arashan.
tash-rabat-kel-suu-ala-kul-11-days: Two days in the saddle to Song-Kul, a night by the Tash-Rabat caravanserai, then off-road to Kok-Kiya and a walk to Kel-Suu. After the south shore of Issyk-Kul you trek to the Altyn-Arashan hot springs and climb to Ala-Kul, a 19 km day on foot.
kyrgyzstan-grand-tour-10-days: Ride for two days from Kyzart to Song-Kul, go off-road to the Kok-Kiya valley and walk to Kel-Suu, then cross to Issyk-Kul. The last three days are on foot: up the Altyn-Arashan gorge, over to Ala-Kul and out to Ak-Suu. Three nights each in yurts, guesthouses and hotels.
song-kul-to-ala-kul-on-horseback-10-days: Ten days, and you ride on every one of them. From Kyzart to Song-Kul and along its shore, then the hills above Issyk-Kul by Boz-Salkyn and Kok-Bulak, a visit to an eagle hunter, and finally up the Altyn-Arashan valley to Ala-Kul. Cars only link the three riding areas.
slow-ride-trek-to-ala-kul-10-days: The unhurried way to do both. Four riding days from Kyzart to Song-Kul and along its western shore, then three days on foot from Altyn-Arashan to Ala-Kul and out. Kyzyl-Oi, the south shore of Issyk-Kul, Chong-Kemin and the Burana tower fill the days between.
kel-suu-chong-kemin-road-trip-10-days: Two nights at Song-Kul, off-road to Kok-Kiya and the walk to Kel-Suu, a lagman cooking stop in Kochkor, the south shore of Issyk-Kul and an off-road climb to the Altyn-Arashan hot springs. A last night in Chong-Kemin breaks the drive back to Bishkek.
song-kul-kok-kiya-kel-suu-9-days: Two days riding from Kyzart to Song-Kul, then a drive south for the off-road day in Kok-Kiya and the walk to Kel-Suu. The second half follows the south shore of Issyk-Kul, with an eagle hunter, the canyons and Jety-Oguz, and ends with the trek to the Altyn-Arashan hot springs.
song-kul-kel-suu-road-trip-9-days: Nine days by road with two nights in a yurt at Song-Kul, so you get a full day by the lake. Then Tash-Bashat, off-road to Kok-Kiya, the walk to Kel-Suu and a night in Naryn, before the south shore of Issyk-Kul and the off-road track to Altyn-Arashan.
kok-kiya-kel-suu-road-trip-8-days: A quick loop by road: one night at Song-Kul, off-road to the Kok-Kiya valley, the walk to Kel-Suu and a night in Naryn. Then you cook lagman in Kochkor, sleep in a yurt by Issyk-Kul, see the south shore and go off-road to Altyn-Arashan.
talas-to-issyk-kul-backroads-8-days: The west of the country first: Talas, Besh-Tash lake, Toktogul and the village of Kyzyl-Oi. Then Ak-Kol and Ming-Kush on the way to two nights at Song-Kul, a night in Tash-Bashat, and a yurt by Issyk-Kul with a lagman lesson in Kochkor, an eagle hunter and the canyons.
song-kul-kel-suu-altyn-arashan-8-days: Eight busy days. Ride from Kyzart over the Jalgyz-Karagai pass to Song-Kul, drive to Tash-Bashat and walk to Kel-Suu, then cross to Issyk-Kul for the south shore. The trip ends on foot, up to the Altyn-Arashan hot springs and out to Ak-Suu.
kyzyl-oi-song-kul-chong-kemin-8-days: Start with a night in Kyzyl-Oi, then ride from Kyzart to Kilemche and on to Song-Kul, with two nights in yurts. After the south shore of Issyk-Kul you trek to Altyn-Arashan and out to Ak-Suu, and finish with a night in Chong-Kemin and a Bishkek city tour.
kol-ukok-to-song-kul-horse-trek-7-days: Seven days in the saddle on trails few groups use. From Kochkor you ride to Kol-Ukok lake, over the Kyzyl-Jar pass to Ak-Kiya, towards the Dolon pass and into the Ken-Suu valley, then over Terskey-Torpu to Song-Kul and out to Kyzart. Five nights in yurts.
kyrgyzstan-overland-road-trip-7-days: A week by road at a brisk pace: a yurt night and a short ride at Song-Kul, Tash-Bashat, the walk to Kel-Suu, then a long drive to Issyk-Kul. You see the south shore and go off-road to Altyn-Arashan before heading back to Bishkek.
two-lakes-kok-bulak-horse-trek-7-days: Ride from Kyzart to Kilemche, over the pass to Song-Kul and along to its western shore. After a guesthouse night by Issyk-Kul you are back in the saddle through the Boz-Salkyn and Kok-Bulak pastures down to Bokonbaev. Seven riding days, five nights in yurts.
song-kul-horse-trek-ala-kul-hike-7-days: Three days on horseback from Kyzart to Song-Kul and back, a day on the south shore of Issyk-Kul, then three days on foot: to the Sirota hut, over to Ala-Kul and down through Altyn-Arashan to Ak-Suu. Runs June to September.
easy-week-song-kul-issyk-kul-7-days: A calm week by road. Two nights in a yurt at Song-Kul with an optional ride, the south shore of Issyk-Kul, an off-road trip up to Altyn-Arashan and a night in Chong-Kemin national park. Walks are short and easy, and it ends with a Bishkek city tour.
talas-to-song-kul-backroads-7-days: A week on the back roads of the west: Talas, Besh-Tash lake, Toktogul and Kyzyl-Oi, with homestay nights along the way. Then Ak-Kol and Ming-Kush lead to two nights with herders at Song-Kul, and you return by Tash-Bashat and Issyk-Kul.
song-kul-kel-suu-in-a-week-7-days: Seven fast days. Ride from Kyzart to Kilemche and on to Song-Kul, drive to Tash-Bashat and walk to Kel-Suu, then follow the south shore of Issyk-Kul back towards Bishkek. Two nights each in yurts, guesthouses and hotels.
ichke-tor-lake-horse-trek-6-days: Six days through country with no tourist camps. Ride from Oro-Bashy to Ichke-Tor lake, on to the Kereshke and Mai-Tor pastures, then to Song-Kul for a full day with herder families. Four nights in yurts and one in a shepherd's house.
kilemche-song-kul-altyn-arashan-6-days: Ride from Kyzart to Kilemche and over the Jalgyz-Karagai pass to Song-Kul, with two nights in yurts. Then the south shore of Issyk-Kul and a two-day trek into Altyn-Arashan and back out. Six days, and you are moving on most of them.
two-lakes-west-shore-horse-trek-6-days: Three days riding from Kyzart to Song-Kul and along to its western shore, a guesthouse night by Issyk-Kul, then two more days in the saddle through the Boz-Salkyn pasture to Bokonbaev. Four nights in yurts.
song-kul-ride-altyn-arashan-trek-5-days: The short version of our ride and trek. One long day on horseback up to Song-Kul, a yurt night, and the ride back to Kyzart. Then the south shore of Issyk-Kul and two days on foot into Altyn-Arashan and out.
kel-suu-issyk-kul-express-5-days: Five days, three lakes. A yurt night at Song-Kul with an optional ride, a night in Tash-Bashat, the 14 km walk to Kel-Suu, then a night by Issyk-Kul on the way home. The drives are long and the scenery earns them.
mai-tor-pastures-horse-trek-5-days: Ride from Epkin to the Kereshke pasture, on to Mai-Tor and over the Jalgyz-Karagai pass to Song-Kul, where you spend a full day with herder families. You leave over the Tuz-Ashuu pass. Three nights in yurts and one in a shepherd's house.
two-lakes-horse-trek-5-days: Ride from Kyzart to Kilemche and over the pass to Song-Kul, then back down and across to Issyk-Kul. The last two days are in the hills above the lake, over the Karaly-Archa pass to Boz-Salkyn and down to Bokonbaev. Three nights in yurts.
song-kul-issyk-kul-road-trip-5-days: A short loop by road: a yurt night at Song-Kul with a ride by the lake, the south shore of Issyk-Kul with an eagle hunter, the canyons and Jety-Oguz, and an off-road trip up to Altyn-Arashan. There are no long hikes.
kel-suu-lake-express-4-days: The fastest way to Kel-Suu. A yurt night at Song-Kul, a drive to Tash-Bashat, the 14 km walk to the lake, and a return by Issyk-Kul. Four days and about 1,080 km on the road.
issyk-kul-altyn-arashan-4-days: Four days around Issyk-Kul. The Burana tower and Kok-Moinok on the way out, an eagle hunter, the canyons and Jety-Oguz on the south shore, then off-road up to Altyn-Arashan for a night in a yurt. Runs from April to November.
song-kul-shoreline-horse-trek-4-days: Four days of riding with no driving at all. From Kyzart to Kilemche, over the Jalgyz-Karagai pass to Song-Kul, a day along the shore to its western end, and back over the Ozbek-Ashuu pass. Three nights in yurts.
family-tour-lakes-eagles-yurts-4-days: An easy four days for all ages: Chong-Kemin national park, the canyons and the shore of Issyk-Kul, a visit to an eagle hunter, and a yurt night up at Song-Kul. There is no trekking, and the riding is optional.
issyk-kul-karakol-canyons-3-days: Three days around Issyk-Kul that run in any season. Drive along the lake to Karakol, come back by the south shore past the canyons to a mountain yurt, and ride half a day to the Shatyly viewpoint before returning to Bishkek.
winter-horse-trek-to-song-kul-3-days: Our one winter trip, from November to April. Ride from Kyzart through the snow to Kilemche, cross the Tuz-Ashuu pass to a frozen Song-Kul, and ride back the next day. One night in a winter homestay and one in a warm yurt.
issyk-kul-song-kul-weekend-3-days: Three days, two lakes: the south shore of Issyk-Kul, a visit to an eagle hunter, then the climb to Song-Kul for a night in a yurt and an optional ride before the drive back to Bishkek.
song-kul-horse-trek-3-days: The classic ride. From Kyzart to Kilemche on day one, over the Jalgyz-Karagai pass to Song-Kul on day two, and back over Tuz-Ashuu on day three. Two nights in yurts, and the trip starts and ends in Kyzart.
song-kul-overnight-horse-trek-2-days: Two days, one night. Ride 22 km from Kyzart up to Song-Kul, sleep in a yurt on the high pasture, and ride back over the Tuz-Ashuu pass. It starts and ends in Kyzart village.
